Rebuild the Nxeon marketing pricing page as a CONDENSED, INTERACTIVE, TABBED single-view — matching a mockup the owner made, but elevated into the site's real theme with animation and conversion psychology. Work ONLY in `/opt/nxeon-wt-pricingv3` (branch feature/pricing-explorer). Commit + push when done. Do NOT run `npm run build`, `prisma generate`, or `prisma db push` (clobbers the live client) — write code and run `npx tsc --noEmit` to typecheck. 

## FIRST: look at the owner's mockup
Read these three frames (JPEGs) — they ARE the required structure:
- `/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/figma_frames/frame_001.jpg` (VPS tab)
- `/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/figma_frames/frame_004.jpg` (Game Servers tab)
- `/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/figma_frames/frame_007.jpg` (Shared Hosting tab)
(Also skim frame_002/003/005/006 in that dir for in-between states.)

## The structure to build (from the mockup)
A single condensed view that fits ~one viewport per product, NOT a long stacked page:
1. **Compact header**: "Nxeon · Pricing" wordmark + tagline "Lock in your price today — it never increases at renewal."
2. **Product tab row** (switches the whole panel, animated): Cloud VPS · Game Servers · Shared Hosting · Business Email · Domains. Each with a small icon; active tab has an underline/glow.
3. **Billing-cycle segmented toggle** (animated, live-updates every price on the panel): Monthly · Annual −10% · Biennial −15% · Triennial −20%, with a muted note "Multi-year applies to VPS only." For NON-VPS products only Monthly + Annual apply — disable/hide 2yr/3yr for them (the mockup's note says so).
4. **Per-product plan panel**:
   - VPS: 4 cards — Starter / Standard (badge "Popular") / Pro / Max (badge "Best value") — CPU / RAM / Storage / Bandwidth rows + "Deploy Now".
   - Game Servers: a row of game-family sub-tabs (Minecraft, Valheim, Rust, Palworld, CS2, Terraria — whatever the DB has) then that family's plan cards (RAM / CPU / Storage / Slots).
   - Shared Hosting: a "First month free · on all plans" badge (HOSTING ONLY) then 3 cards (Disk / Websites / Databases / Bandwidth / Mailboxes).
   - Business Email: mailbox plans (cards).
   - Domains: a TLD price grid (POPULAR_TLDS — keep them labelled "indicative").
5. **"Included with all plans" strip** (product-specific checklist — see the frames).
6. **Trust footer**: DDoS protected · Prepaid wallet, cancel anytime · Auto backups · NVMe everywhere · Free migration assistance.
Each plan card's CTA ("Deploy Now") links where the current pricing page's CTAs link (check the existing page / homepage for the correct deploy/order href per product).

## THEME — this is critical (prior redesigns were REJECTED for being off-theme)
The mockup is black/green — DO NOT copy that palette. Use the site's REAL theme from `app/globals.css` (READ IT). It is: deep NAVY ground (`--color-navy-950 #060a14`), VIOLET brand (`--color-brand-500 #6f47f5`, `--color-brand-400 #8a70fb`), BLUE + CYAN accents (`--color-accent-blue #3b82f6`, `--color-accent-cyan #22d3ee`), glass cards, violet glow. Use existing utilities: `grad-text`, `.card`, `.btn-primary`/`.btn-secondary`, `.eyebrow`/`.eyebrow-pill`, `hero-aura`, `tone-panel`/`tone-deep`, `.rail`, and `Reveal`/`AmbientField` from `components/marketing/`. **"Popular" badge = violet; "Best value" badge + the active/live pops = CYAN. NEVER amber** (amber only as a semantic warning). Study `app/page.tsx` and existing `components/marketing/*` to match the aesthetic exactly. It must look like it belongs to the same product as the navy/violet dashboard.

## Make it PREMIUM + INTERACTIVE (the owner explicitly asked for this)
- The page must be a **client component** (or a server component that fetches data + passes it to a client `PricingExplorer` component you create in `components/marketing/`). Interactive state: selected product tab, billing cycle, selected game family.
- **Animated price transitions** when the billing cycle changes (e.g. a quick fade/slide or count feel via CSS transition on the number) — prices should visibly update.
- Smooth **tab-switch animation** for the product panel (fade/slide in). Hover micro-interactions on cards (lift/glow). Use CSS transitions/keyframes — there is NO motion library installed, so do not import framer-motion/gsap.
- Add at least one **screen-animation / interactive widget** that reinforces value: e.g. reuse a showcase component (`components/marketing/showcase/ServerDashboard.tsx`, `GameControlPanel.tsx`, `DeployCard.tsx` hero terminal) or a small live "effective $/mo · you save $X/yr" readout that animates with the toggle. Tasteful, on-brand, not gaudy.
- `AmbientField` dot-field background + `hero-aura` glow for depth. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Must be fully responsive / mobile-first (tabs collapse gracefully; cards stack).

## Conversion psychology (research-backed — bake these in)
- Anchor with 4 VPS tiers but visually push the middle: **Standard = "Most popular"** (violet, raised, brightest CTA); **Max = "Best value"** high anchor (cyan) so Standard feels smart.
- **Annual pre-selected** by default (not Monthly). For each term show the effective $/mo AND the savings framed as DOLLARS ("save $X/yr"), not only a bare %. Longer term = bigger saving, clearly shown — the goal is to provoke longer commitments.
- Reinforce **"the price you sign up at is the price you renew at"** and **no lock-in, cancel anytime** near the CTAs (trust removes friction).
- Include a compact **social-proof / ★★★★★** element (reuse an existing reviews component if present, e.g. `CustomerReviews`/`ReviewBadges`; otherwise a small modest star strip — do NOT fabricate specific company names or metrics).
- Value-stack via the "included with all plans" strip. Keep it tight (condensed) — reduce choice paralysis.

## HARD honesty rules (the owner audits these — do not break)
- EVERY price MUST be DB-fed through the existing queries (`db.plan` / `db.gamePlan` / `db.hostingPlan` / `db.emailPlan`) and priced with the real `termPriceCents(monthlyCents, months, annualDiscountPct)` from `lib/billing-terms.ts` (it is a pure, client-safe fn) + the live `annualDiscountPct()`. **Zero hard-coded plan prices.** Displayed === charged: the /mo you show for a term must equal what checkout charges for that term. Reuse the existing page's data-fetching (it already loads every product + `POPULAR_TLDS`).
- **First-month-free is SHARED-HOSTING ONLY** (gate with the existing `firstMonthFreeAppliesTo("HOSTING")`). The "First month free" badge appears ONLY on the Hosting tab. NEVER show $0 / free-month on VPS, Game, or Email.
- Multi-year (Biennial/Triennial) is VPS-only — non-VPS products show only Monthly/Annual.
- No invented stats, no "24/7 support" (monitoring only), TLD prices stay "indicative".

## Output
- Replace `app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx` (keep it a server component that loads data) and add `components/marketing/PricingExplorer.tsx` (the "use client" interactive panel) + any small sub-components. Keep the page's existing `metadata`/SEO.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` must be clean (report the result).
- Commit + push to `origin/feature/pricing-explorer`.
- Report: the section-by-section result, which brand tokens/components/animations you used, how the live pricing math stays displayed===charged, and confirm first-month-free is hosting-only + every price DB-fed. This will be previewed on staging before going live — make it genuinely premium and true to the mockup's condensed structure.

1	/**
2	 * Billing term definitions + discount math, shared by ordering, renewal,
3	 * the deploy wizard, invoices and the domain flow. Discounts are the platform's
4	 * promo (longer commitment = cheaper); tune here (or later via admin Settings).
5	 */
6	
7	export type VpsTerm = { months: number; label: string; short: string; discountPct: number };
8	
9	/** The ANNUAL term is 12 months — the one term whose discount is admin-configurable. */
10	export const ANNUAL_TERM_MONTHS = 12;
11	
12	/**
13	 * The annual (12-month) commitment discount SHIPPED as the default, and the fallback
14	 * for the `annual_discount_percent` admin setting (lib/annual-discount.ts).
15	 *
16	 * It MUST equal the 12-month `VPS_TERMS` discountPct below: a platform whose
17	 * `Setting` table has no `annual_discount_percent` row must price the annual term
18	 * EXACTLY as it did before the setting existed, so no existing annual server's
19	 * renewal price moves the moment this wiring lands. The setting only ever raises or
20	 * lowers it deliberately, from the admin Billing panel.
21	 */
22	export const DEFAULT_ANNUAL_DISCOUNT_PCT = 10;
23	
24	export const VPS_TERMS: VpsTerm[] = [
25	  { months: 1, label: "Monthly", short: "1 mo", discountPct: 0 },
26	  // Annual is admin-configurable — this is only the SHIPPED default. Every charge
27	  // path resolves the live rate via `annualDiscountPct()` and passes it through
28	  // `vpsTermPriceCents`; this constant is what an un-wired caller (and a 2-arg call)
29	  // falls back to. Keep it === DEFAULT_ANNUAL_DISCOUNT_PCT.
30	  { months: 12, label: "Annual", short: "1 yr", discountPct: DEFAULT_ANNUAL_DISCOUNT_PCT },
31	  { months: 24, label: "Biennial", short: "2 yr", discountPct: 15 },
32	  { months: 36, label: "Triennial", short: "3 yr", discountPct: 20 },
33	];
34	
35	export function vpsTerm(months: number): VpsTerm {
36	  return VPS_TERMS.find((t) => t.months === months) ?? VPS_TERMS[0];
37	}
38	
39	/**
40	 * The discount percent to apply to a term.
41	 *
42	 * For the ANNUAL (12-month) term this is admin-configurable: pass the
43	 * `annualDiscountPct` resolved from the `annual_discount_percent` setting
44	 * (lib/annual-discount.ts) and it WINS over the shipped default. Every other term
45	 * keeps its fixed `VPS_TERMS` rate. Omitting the override — or passing a
46	 * non-finite value — falls back to the shipped default, so a 2-arg
47	 * `vpsTermPriceCents` call and any caller that has not been wired up price annual at
48	 * `DEFAULT_ANNUAL_DISCOUNT_PCT`, i.e. exactly what the platform shipped before.
49	 * Clamped to 0..90 here as a second line of defence behind the setting reader.
50	 */
51	export function termDiscountPct(months: number, annualDiscountPct?: number): number {
52	  if (months === ANNUAL_TERM_MONTHS && annualDiscountPct != null && Number.isFinite(annualDiscountPct)) {
53	    return Math.min(90, Math.max(0, annualDiscountPct));
54	  }
55	  return vpsTerm(months).discountPct;
56	}
57	
58	/**
59	 * Total charge (cents) for a plan over a term, discount applied.
60	 *
61	 * `annualDiscountPct` (optional) overrides the ANNUAL term's discount with the
62	 * admin-configured rate; see `termDiscountPct`. It is the ONE knob that makes
63	 * annual billing configurable while keeping this the single price formula —
64	 * displayed (deploy wizard), charged (lib/order.ts) and renewed (renewalCharge)
65	 * all call this with the SAME resolved rate, so they cannot disagree.
66	 */
67	export function vpsTermPriceCents(monthlyCents: number, months: number, annualDiscountPct?: number): number {
68	  const pct = termDiscountPct(months, annualDiscountPct);
69	  return Math.round(monthlyCents * months * (1 - pct / 100));
70	}
71	
72	/**
73	 * Generic term price — the product-agnostic name for the ONE term formula above.
74	 * Shared Hosting, Business Email, Game servers and NxCloud all price a term as
75	 * `monthlyCents × months × (1 − annualDiscount)` exactly the way a VPS does, so
76	 * they call THIS and there is a single arithmetic for every product+term. It is a
77	 * thin alias of `vpsTermPriceCents` on purpose: the annual discount is resolved
78	 * once (order) and re-resolved (renewal) against the SAME setting, so
79	 * displayed === charged === renewed holds for every product.
80	 */
81	export function termPriceCents(monthlyCents: number, months: number, annualDiscountPct?: number): number {
82	  return vpsTermPriceCents(monthlyCents, months, annualDiscountPct);
83	}
84	
85	/**
86	 * The terms offered on the NON-VPS products (Shared Hosting, Business Email, Game
87	 * servers, NxCloud): Monthly and Annual only. VPS additionally sells 24/36-month
88	 * terms via `VPS_TERMS`; the other products keep the choice to the two the
89	 * customer actually reasons about, and the Annual term is the ONE admin-configurable
90	 * discount (see `annualDiscountPct()`).
91	 */
92	export const PRODUCT_TERMS: VpsTerm[] = [VPS_TERMS[0], VPS_TERMS[1]];
93	
94	/**
95	 * Clamp any term input from a product order form to a SUPPORTED product term —
96	 * Annual (12) if exactly 12 was chosen, else Monthly (1). A malformed / unlisted
97	 * value can therefore only ever fall back to the cheapest (monthly) term, never
98	 * grant a longer paid term the customer did not pay for.
99	 */
100	export function normalizeProductTerm(months: unknown): number {
101	  const m = Math.round(Number(months));
102	  return m === ANNUAL_TERM_MONTHS ? ANNUAL_TERM_MONTHS : 1;
103	}
104	
105	/**
106	 * Effective monthly-equivalent price after the term discount (for "$/mo" display).
107	 *
108	 * `months <= 0` returns the undiscounted monthly price rather than dividing by it.
109	 * This is not display hygiene — it is a money guard. `prorateDeltaCents`
110	 * (lib/proration.ts) prices BOTH halves of every upgrade and downgrade credit
111	 * through this function using `Server.termMonths`, and a 0 there made the division
112	 * `0 / 0` → NaN, which sails through `Math.round`, through `Math.max(0, delta)`
113	 * (NaN is not > 0, so the clamp returns NaN, not 0) and into `debitWallet` as the
114	 * amount to take. The result is a charge that either explodes at the database or,
115	 * on the credit side, writes NaN where a customer's balance used to be. The column
116	 * defaults to 1 and every writer clamps to >= 1 today, so this is a latch, not a
117	 * live bug — but a shared money function must not have a NaN in it.
118	 */
119	export function vpsEffectiveMonthly(monthlyCents: number, months: number, annualDiscountPct?: number): number {
120	  if (!Number.isFinite(months) || months <= 0) return Math.round(monthlyCents);
121	  return Math.round(vpsTermPriceCents(monthlyCents, months, annualDiscountPct) / months);
122	}
123

125	
126	export const DOMAIN_TERMS: DomainTerm[] = [
127	  { years: 1, label: "1 year", discountPct: 0 },
128	  { years: 2, label: "2 years", discountPct: 5 },
129	  { years: 3, label: "3 years", discountPct: 10 },
130	];
131	
132	export function domainTerm(years: number): DomainTerm {
133	  return DOMAIN_TERMS.find((t) => t.years === years) ?? DOMAIN_TERMS[0];
134	}
135	
136	/** Total charge (cents) for a domain over N years, discount applied. */
137	export function domainTermPriceCents(perYearCents: number, years: number): number {
138	  const t = domainTerm(years);
139	  return Math.round(perYearCents * years * (1 - t.discountPct / 100));
140	}

Push succeeded — `3b00eb3..47135e5` is now on `origin/feature/pricing-explorer`. All seven refinements are done, `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean (exit 0).

## Refinement pass — what changed, per item

1. **Domains: toggle removed + search added.** The billing-cycle segmented control now renders only when `product !== "domains"` (domains are per-year only). The Domains panel got the live `<DomainChecker compact />` marketing search widget (self-contained client component, the same one `/domains` uses — no `configured` prop needed) above the "indicative" TLD grid.

2. **Footer logo blur fixed.** `components/marketing/MarketingFooter.tsx` `<Image src="/logo.png">` now uses the asset's true intrinsic `width={496} height={85}` (confirmed via `identify`: 496×85), keeping `className="h-[38px] w-auto object-contain"`, so Next serves a crisp source instead of a ~4× upscale.

3. **"Included with all plans" centered** — the strip is now `text-center` with a `justify-center` checklist row.

4. **Interactive VPS add-on builder ("Build your server").** Base-plan chips (defaults to the popular tier) + an **extra-storage slider** (0–200 GB, step `EXTRA_DISK_STEP_GB`) priced with `extraDiskCentsAt(gb, perGbCents)` + a **daily-backups (Plus) toggle** priced from `backupPlusMonthlyCents()`. The server page now fetches `backupPlusMonthlyCents()` and `extraDiskPerGbCents()` (alongside `annualDiscountPct()`) and passes them down. A live "Your build $X/mo" readout re-computes and pops on every change, with a per-line breakdown, add-ons clearly labelled as recurring monthly on top of the plan. VPS-only, as instructed.

5. **Animated per-tab screens.** Added a `ProductScreen` that swaps by tab: `ServerDashboard` (VPS + Hosting), `GameControlPanel` (Game), `MailInbox` (Email) — all reused showcase components, motion-safe. On VPS it sits beside the add-on builder; on other products it's centered.

6. **Trustpilot + Google review logos.** `<ReviewBadges />` (Trustpilot · HostAdvice · Google, the same homepage component) is rendered server-side and passed into the explorer header, replacing the plain ★★★★★ line.

7. **Per-service accent glow/color.** An `ACCENTS` map (all literal Tailwind class strings + inline rgba glows/auras so nothing is dynamically constructed) threads a hue through the active tab underline/glow, toggle thumb, panel aura, game sub-tab pill, popular badge/ring/CTA and the savings readout: **VPS=violet, Game=emerald, Hosting=cyan, Email=blue, Domains=indigo→fuchsia** — no amber anywhere.

## Honesty rules still hold
- **Displayed === charged:** every plan `$/mo` still runs the DB monthly through `termPriceCents`/`vpsEffectiveMonthly`; the new add-ons use `extraDiskCentsAt(perGbCents)` and the admin-resolved `backupPlusMonthlyCents()` — the exact figures `lib/order.ts` bills. Zero hard-coded prices.
- **First-month-free stays HOSTING-ONLY** via the nullable `hostingPromoLabel` gated on `firstMonthFreeAppliesTo("HOSTING")`; the badge only renders in the hosting branch.
- Multi-year remains VPS-only (toggle hidden for domains; `PRODUCT_TERMS` for the rest). TLDs stay "indicative".
- **Not regressed:** condensed tabbed layout, Annual pre-selected default, and the Standard=Most-popular (violet) / Max=Best-value (cyan) anchoring are all intact.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; committed as `47135e5` and pushed to `origin/feature/pricing-explorer`. (Did not run `npm build`/`prisma`, per rules.)

One note for the staging preview: `<ReviewBadges />` shows its clearly-labelled demo placeholder (Trustpilot/HostAdvice/Google) until real approved external reviews exist in the DB — it auto-switches to real badges when they do; no fabricated figures are introduced by this change.
